Commentary.Commentary: That brings us to the end of today's action and this series! Australia have clinched this trophy outsmarting West Indies and the South Africans. Next up, the Kangaroos will travel to Sri Lanka whereas the Caribbean team will host India for a Test series. Elsewhere, join us on the 29th of June for the 4th ODI between England and Sri Lanka to be played in London at 1730 IST for some more cricketing action. Until next time, take care and ciao!

Australia captain, STEVEN SMITH thinks that they were in trouble at one point but Wade and their tail did extemely well to get them to a fighting total on the board. Adds that it's pleasing that they usually play so well in finals. Says they want to keep winning and keep improving. Says that Justin Langer is an experienced coach and he's done well for Western Australia. Thinks that Barbados is great and the support has been amazing.

Man of the Series, JOSH HAZLEWOOD says that their bowling unit is working great together and praises Mitchell Marsh. Adds that the pitch got slower and credits Zampa for his bowling and picking the wicket of Pollard. Says that he is very happy with his 5-fer and he tries to keep it simple.

West Indies captain, JASON HOLDER says that they weren't that well in the field and conceded a few runs too many and they never really recovered from that. Admits that the wickets of Smith and Maxwell in the 31st over of the first innings changed the game totally and they missed Gabriel in the death overs. Credits Gabriel and thinks they have put up some good performances leading to this final. Adds that  they got 2 hundreds in this series (Samuels and Bravo) and Pollard's presence and his experience has been key. Says that the India series is a big one and they have time to recover.

Man of the Match, MITCHELL MARSH says that every series he plays for his country is something to cherish about and it was important to win. Adds that he hadn't taken a wicket all series and it was nice to take a few today. Thinks that getting the opportunity to bowl upfront today was nice. Further says they tried to make use of the pitch conditions. Thinks that West Indies have had a great series and have played some amazing cricket. Australia were eyeing for the top order wickets which paved their way to victory.

Josh Hazlewood, with his 2nd 5-fer in ODIs wreaked havoc for the Kangaroos. Partnering him well was Mitchell Marsh who at one stage had figures of 7-1-8-3. Nathan Coulter-Nile and Adam Zampa shared a wicket as well. In the first innings, after Finch's and Smith's knock, Wade's unbeaten 57 clearly had a major role to play in today's result. Join us in a while for the presentation.

West Indies, after a superb opening stand lost their way with quick wickets in the middle. Charles missed out on his fifty whereas Ramdin's late surge wasn't enough to take his team home. The big three playing down the order - Pollard, Holder and Brathwaite failed to come good on such a big occasion.

What a clinical performance this has been from Australia to clinch this tri-series. They have cleared aside the West Indian resistance and managed to outclass the hosts in front of their home crowd. Two people made all the difference for Australia - Matthew Wade with the bat when his team was staring down the barrel and Mitchell Marsh with the ball, picking up early wickets.

OUT! AUSTRALIA ARE THE TRI-SERIES CHAMPIONS! Josh Hazlewood gets his second ODI 5-wicket haul. He has to give credit for this wicket to Glenn Maxwell. What an outstanding catch. Hazlewood keeps this very full on middle, 134.3 kph, Benn lofts this over wide long on. Glenn Maxwell is stationed at the boundary, he watches the ball come to him, senses it well, leaps at the right moment and takes a very good catch. It is referred upstairs and replays confirm that Maxwell is just fine. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 58 RUNS!
Full and just outside off, 133.4 kph, Gabriel flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
SHANNON GABRIEL is the last man in, replacing Narine.
OUT! That is the 9th one down. Australia inch closer. Landed outside off, 134.2 kph, Narine backs away and lofts it over covers but Steven Smith over there leaps and takes a good catch.
Landed outside off, 134.3 kph, Benn looks to heave it away but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat to wide mid on. A single taken.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
FOUR! Down the leg side, 145 kph, Narine tickles it past the diving Wade to the fine leg fence!
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, 144.6 kph, left alone.
FOUR! Excellent yorker on middle, 144.2 kph, Narine looks to dig it out but the ball goes between his legs past the leg stump to the fine leg fence!
Short and outside off, 144.2 kph, punched to deep cover for a couple.
MITCHELL STARC comes back on to finish off things.
DROPPED! Another tough chance, put down. Full on middle, 132.6 kph, Narine smashes it back to the bowler who sticks out his right hand but it deflects to cover.
FOUR! The strokes keep coming! A short ball outside off, 132.5 kph, Narine pulls it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary!
Landed outside off, 137.4 kph, Benn is squared up as he looks to defend and the ball goes off the outside edge to third man. A single taken.
Big SULIEMAN BENN walks in at number 10, replacing Ramdin.

OUT! The middle stump is pegged back and Australia scent a sight of a win close by. Full and straight, you miss I hit, Ramdin is the second person pronoun and Hazlewood is the 'I'. Ramdin swings but misses and Hazlewood hits. That might be it for the home side. 77 needed from 39 balls now.

Short and outside off, angling in, 136.4 kph, Sunil goes for the pull but the ball goes off the inside edge onto his pads and deflects to third man where Matthew Wade dives to his left to stop the ball. A single taken.
A bouncer outside off, 131.4 kph, Narine lets it go, thinking it will be wided but it isn't.

Comes down the track and hammers it back to the bowler. 6 runs from the over, Marsh finishes with figures of 10-1-32-3, might be the decisive one as far as the Man Of The Match award is concerned. Of course, assuming that Australia win from here...
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.

FOUR! He is not going to stick around and no point in doing so. Seeing off all the 50 overs will not improve the net run rate after the final for the next series. Short and outside off, Narine backs away and slaps it over covers for a boundary. 78 more needed from 44 balls now.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

ALMOST A RUN OUT! Landed outside off, 122.6 kph, Narine punches this back. Marsh collects and tries to deflect it back on to the stumps but it goes away to mid off. Ramdin was backing up a bit too far.
A short ball outside off, 129.7 kph, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Excellent fielding by Finch. Full toss on middle, Narine flicks it through mid-wicket. The ball races to the ropes where Aaron Finch gets across, tumbles but manages to pull it in. It is referred upstairs but replays show that Finch is clean. 4 runs and a wicket from the over, Hazlewood has figures of 8-1-41-2.
Full on middle, 132.9 kph, Narine hammers this through mid on where Mitchell Starc makes a terrific stop.
On a good length around off, angling in, Narine plays inside the line and is beaten.
SUNIL NARINE walks in at number 9, replacing Brathwaite.

OUT! BOWLED! That silences the crowd. Hazlewood keeps this on a length and very straight, 135.9 kph, Brathwaite goes for the pull but misses and that hits the timber. Hazlewood is pumped up. The Aussies realize that it could be a big wicket. 86 MORE NEEDED FROM 51 balls now...
Short and outside off, 135.6 kph, punched through the covers for a run.
On middle, 132.5 kph, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD is back on.
A short ball outside off, 135.3 kph, Denesh goes for the pull but gets a bottom edge on the bounce to the keeper. Ramdin is furious with himself.
WIDE. A bouncer now, outside off, 131.3 kph, Ramdin watches it sail over his head and it is signalled a wide!

OVERTHROWS. The crowd is now getting into it. Ramdin pushes it towards short mid-wicket, takes a start but then sends Brathwaite back. The non-striker has to dive in but Bailey misses his shy at the bowler's end. Could have been close as per the replays but instead, overthrows are conceded as the ball goes all the way to the sweeper cover boundary. 89 more needed from 55 balls now.

SIX! Superb shot! The game is right here in the balance. Yes, the hosts are 6 wickets down. Yes, they need at over 10 an over. But remember, they are double WT20 champions, so scoring 100 off the last 10 is not impossible, if wickets are in hand. Full and outside off, 128 kph, Ramdin gets under it and lofts it over long off for a biggie!
Whips this over mid-wicket and gets a couple.
A short ball on middle and off, 132.5 kph, pulled down to wide long on for a run. 99 more needed from 58 balls now.
Landed outside off, 120.3 kph, pushed to point for a single.
MITCHELL MARSH comes back into the attack.
POWERPLAY 3! Five fielders are now allowed outside the circle.
SIX! There she goes! Short of a length delivery on off. Brathwaite pulls it high in the air and murders it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum. 12 runs off the over.
Landed on off on a good length, Brathwaite is cramped for room as he ends up defending it back to NCN.
Slower bouncer outside off, Brathwaite goes for a wild pull but fails to connect.
Short of a length around off, Ramdin pushes it to cover-point and picks up a run.
Wide outside off, Brathwaite runs it down to third man on a bounce for a single.
Shortish outside off, steered to third man for a single.
TWO WIDES! Fires it short and down the leg side, Brathwaite looks to pull it away but misses out. The umpire signals it a wide.
WIDE! A slower delivery down the leg side. Wide called by the umpire.
Back of a length outside off, chopped straight to backward point.

DROPPED! Length delivery around off, Barthwaite gets on his knees and paddles it towards fine leg. Starc at short fine leg drops another change, although it was tough this time around. Manages to save a certain boundary and allows just a run.
FOUR! Shortish outside off, Brathwaite slaps it just wide of the mid off fielder for a boundary. That was powerfully hit by the lanky West Indian.
Ramdin cuts the length delivery through square of the wicket on the off side for a run.
Short and outside off, Ramdin tries to smash hardbut gets beaten.

What happened there? Full and on middle and leg, Ramdin flicks it in the air off his front foot. The ball travels high in the air towards fine leg. Starc looks to get under it but was lost under the lights and lets it go for a boundary. It could have been a regulation catch but it's not to be as all Hazlewood can do is smile!
Good length delivery around off, Brathwaite fails to connect on that one.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
CARLOS BRATHWAITE is the new man in.

OUT! With the asking rate climbing Holder holes out! Back of a length outside off, Holder swings his bat but miscues it. The ball skies in the air and Finch at sweeper cover pouches a reverse-cup catch. That's a timely wicket for the Aussies. WI are 123 away now.
WIDE! Fires it down the leg side to be called a wide.
Good comeback! Short and wide outside oof, Holder taps it to Maxwell at point.
FOUR! Captain taking on the charge! On a length around off, Holder has ample of room to clobber it over mid on for a biggie.
Landed outside off, Holder inside edges it onto his pads.
Slower bouncer on off, Ramdin leaves it alone but surprisingly the umpire doesn't call it a wide.
Full ball outside off, Ramdin drives it to mid off. Runs not coming easy for West Indies.
Ramdin shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Wide outside off, Holder steers it to third man for a single.

NOT OUT! On middle and leg, Ramdin nudges it to the leg side and sets off. Bailey comes charging in and disturbs the stumps at the striker's end with a direct hit. The umpires go upstairs but replays confirm Holder dragging his bat in time.
Third umpire is referred for a run out appeal.
Holder plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man for a single.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD replaces Marsh now.
DROPPED! Half chance though! On a length around off, Ramdin slaps it straight down the ground as NCN gets his left hand to it on his followthrough. He hopes for it to stick but that doesn't happen.
Shortish on middle, Randin closes the face of his blade and tucks it to short mid-wicket. There is a direct hit at the striker's end but Ramdin was well in.
Ramdin drives the length delivery straight to mid on.
Holder blocks the good length delivery to the off side for a run.
Another shortish delivery outside off, Holder opens the face of his bat and works it to third man for a brace.
Short of a length around off, angling in. Holder hops and blocks it.
NATHAN COULTER-NILE comes back on.
On a length around off, Ramdin tucks it to the leg side.
Fullish delivery on middle, Holder clips it just  wide of short mid-wicket for a single.
Wide outside off, punched through cover-point for a brace.
Full and on off, Holder pushes it to short cover.
Ramdin cuts the length delivery around off to point and picks up another swift run.
Good length on middle, defended to mid-wicket for a single.
Shortish around off, slammed to long on for a single. Zampa finishes, 10-0-50-1.
Jason has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Inside out and over! Leg spinner on middle, Holder lofts it over covers for a boundary.
Holder has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker outside off, Holder swings his bat to smash it to the leg side but gets a leading edge just short of point.
Pitched up on off, Holder blocks it.
Back of a length around off, Ramdin steers it to Maxwell at point. Just a single from that over. Marsh's figures read, 7-1-8-3.
Full ball on off, flicked away to short mid-wicket for no run.
Bouncer around off, Ramdin ducks under it to evade.
Short and outside off, cut away to point.
Fuller and outside off, Ramdin gets across and works it to the leg side for no run.
Landed outside off, Holder opens the face of his bat and plays it to point for a run.
MITCHELL MARSH comes back on.
Holder pushes the loopy delivery to covers and picks up a quick single. Holder looks in pain as he seems to have pulled his hamsting...
Shortish outside off, punched through the off side for a single.
Pitched up on off, Ramdin blocks it leaning on his front foot.
Floated around off, Holder pushes and gets it through covers for a single.
Holder has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted delivery around off, spinning away. Denesh goes hard at it but miscues it over covers for a run. Catch it was the call from Zampa which went unanswered.
Serves it wide outside off, Holder fails to connect as Wade collects it nicely.
FOUR! Much, much needed! Full and outside off, Holder slices it over backward point to fetch a boundary for himself.
Play and a miss! Fullish delivery way outside off, Holder looks for a crisp cover drive but misses out. A little bit of reverse swing on that occasion.
Holder blocks the length delivery on off with ease.
Full and on the pads, worked to the leg side for a single.
Full and on off, Ramdin punches it to Starc on a bounce.
67 runs for the loss of 5 wickets in the last 20 overs. That's a big dent in the West Indian run chase! Australia were 151/3 at this stage, just before that Gabriel's double-blow over.
Full on middle, 84.9 kph, driven back to the bowler.
Floated again, this is on off, 81.5 kph, Denesh leans and pushes it to long off for one.
Nicely tossed up around middle, 80.3 kph, Holder leans and pushes it to long off for a run.
Outside off, 83.8 kph, pushed to backward point.
Tossed up around off, 76.1 kph, pushed down to long off for a single.
IN THE AIR, SHORT! Floated outside off, 78.5 kph, Ramdin leans to drive but it is uppish and nearly carries to Steven Smith at short extra cover who dives and parries it to the bowler.
Landed outside off, swings in late, 139.3 kph, flicked through mid-wicket for a run. 159 more needed from 126 balls now.
A bouncer now on middle, 141.4 kph, ducked under.
Landed on middle, 138.8 kph, Ramdin taps it to the leg side and sets off but it is barely past the bowler and Holder sends his vice captain back.
Full and wide outside off, steered to third man for a single.
Angled in from outside off, 145.6 kph, left alone.
Full and outside off, 143.6 kph, almost a yorker, well dug out.
Tossed up outside off, 81.2 kph, Ramdin comes forward and lets it go. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, Zampa has figures of 7-0-38-1.
Another googly, outside off, 80.4 kph, pushed to point for a single.
The wrong 'un on middle, well defended.
FOUR! Brilliant! Tossed up outside off, 78.8 kph, Holder leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! No slow starters this time. Last game, he took 17 balls to get off the mark.
Floated on middle, 86.2 kph, Holder lunges to defend.
JASON HOLDER walks in at number 7, replacing Pollard. West Indies need a partnership here.

OUT! That is a splendid catch from Hazlewood and Pollard is out of here! The big man's all-or-nothing approach does not last long. Zampa tosses this one well outside off, 81 kph, Pollard gets underneath it and drives it flat over mid off. It seems like he has got the distance but Josh Hazlewood covers good ground to his left from long off, dives full stretch and takes a really decent catch! The Aussies are all over Zampa. They know what a big wicket this is. A decent stand is broken as well. 166 NOW NEEDED FROM 137 BALLS.
Down the leg side, 146.3 kph, Pollard misses his tuck and the ball goes off his hips to square leg. A leg bye taken.
Full and slightly wide outside off, pushed behind point for one.
Starc shifts to around the wicket for Ramdin.
Down the leg side, 146.3 kph, flicked to fine leg for a run.
Smith walks across to Starc and asks him to change the angle. Coming from over the wicket now.
Very full on off, swinging in, 144.9 kph, Pollard works it off the inside half of the bat through mid-wicket. Gets a couple. 169 more needed from 141 balls now.
Angles back in from outside off, 144.2 kph, Pollard defends it watchfully.

Full and outside off, 144.5 kph, angling down the leg side, Ramdin falls over in his attempt to flick and is hit on the pads. There is a muted appeal for LBW which is turned down. A single taken. Leg bye signalled. 100 IS UP FOR THE WEST INDIES.
Full and outside off, turning away, 83.6 kph, pushed to point. 11 from the over!

SIX! Just over! The big man has decided to go for it now. Short and outside off, 83.3 kph, Pollard goes back and pulls it over long on. It is a flat hit and Nathan Coulter-Nile thinks he has a chance at the boundary and leaps but the ball clears him!
Floated around leg stump, 81.4 kph, Kieron lunges to block.

FOUR! There goes the big man! Tossed up on middle, 82.4 kph, Pollard swings it cleanly over mid on and beats the fielder at long on! He is struggling to take the singles, so he might as well go for broke here. 178 more needed from 147 balls now.
A full toss outside off, 80.3 kph, Ramdin leans and drives it to long off for a single.
Floated on middle, 78.6 kph, watchfully defended.
A yorker outside off, dug out to point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

That is a massive indipper from Starc. Pollard is beaten by it as he looks to drive and is hit on the pads. Starc appeals long and hard but umpire Kettleborough is firm and shakes his head. Smith asks his bowler about where he hit, whether the impact was outside off. Not quite sure what Starc answered because the camera was panned on Smith. Eventually the review was not taken and replays detected a massive inside edge. Seems like Pollard indicated to the Aussies that he had an inside edge. After all, it is a gentleman's game. He helped his dear friend Starc out there.
On middle and off, 141.4 kph, worked through square leg for a single.

Oooh.... right on the money first ball. On a length outside off, 145.2 kph, nips back in sharply, Ramdin is caught in his crease as he looks to defend and is hit on the pads. Starc starts to appeal but then bails out almost instantaneously. Replays reveal an inside edge.
Pollard seems all ready now. MITCHELL STARC is back on.
Looks like Pollard has some issue here. He has signalled to the dressing room for something. The physio is out in the middle.

Shortish on middle and off, whipped over mid-wicket for a couple. Good sliding stop by Nathan Coulter-Nile at the boundary. Excellent over for the Windies, 9 from it. Just the momentum shift they needed.
This one lands on middle, spins away sharply, 83.8 kph, Pollard defends watchfully.
Down the leg side, 85.6 kph, worked behind square leg for an easy couple.
Short again, outside off, 85.6 kph, cut to deep point for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.

EDGED! FOUR! Where is the slip? Surprising from Smith. Both batsmen are relatively new but he has not kept a slip. Short and outside off, Ramdin goes back to cut but is too close to the ball and gets a thick outside edge. It goes behind but the slip cordon is vacant and the ball runs away to the third man fence! 189 more needed from 161 balls.
A length ball wide outside off, 129.4 kph, a slash and a miss from the big man. Just a run from the over, 3 in the last 2.
On a good length outside off, 130.9 kph, defended with a nice little hop.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a good length around off, 131.5 kph, Ramdin looks to tuck it to the leg side but gets a leading edge behind point. A single taken.
On a good length outside off, 127.5 kph, Denesh plays into this one and is beaten.
A short ball outside off, angling in, 129.2 kph, Ramdin ducks.
Full and outside off, pushed past the bowler to long off for one.
Punches this off the back foot through the covers for a run.
Finally gets this short one away, pushing through the covers for a single.
Another short ball, turning away, 80.6 kph, pushed once more to cover.
Shorter in length, 81.9 kph, punched to cover again.
Tossed up outside off, 83.4 kph, driven straight to short cover.
Full on middle, 129.4 kph, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple. Just 2 runs and a wicket from the over, Marsh now has figures of 5-1-6-3! Just 24/3 in the last 10 overs.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Walks down the track, Marsh bowls it really full outside off, 135.9 kph, Kieron looks to squeeze it to third man but misses.
Landed outside off, 129 kph, Pollard shoulders arms but the ball bounces high and hits the bottom edge to go to backward point.
KIERON POLLARD walks in at number 6, replacing Charles.

OUT! LBW! Third wicket for Marsh and he is on a roll here! Full and straight, 123.3 kph, Charles misses his flick and is hit on the front pad. Marsh roars out an appeal, umpire Kettleborough takes his time and raises his finger! Charles is disappointed. He despairingly looks at Ramdin for a possible review but is asked to go on his way. Perhaps he knew it. He trudges back. Another half century missed. That is his third score in the range of 40-50 in the last 5 innings. Hawk Eye shows that to be hitting leg stump. West Indies have now lost 4/23 in 59 balls. 199 MORE NEEDED FROM 171 BALLS NOW.
Flatter and outside off, Charles runs it down to third man for a single.
Shortish outside off, punched to deep point for a run.
Down the leg side, Ramdin fails to connect and the ball kisses his thigh pad.
Loopy on off, pushed to short cover for no run.
Flatter delivery around off, driven to extra cover for a run.
Pitched up on middle, Charles drives it straight down the ground as Zampa again dives to save a run.
Serves a length delivery on off, Ramdin watchfully blocks it. Another successful over for the Aussies.
On length around off, Ramdin defends it.
Short of a length on off, Ramdin goes hard at it but misses out.
Free Hit coming up...
NO BALL! Bouncer on off, Ramdin leaves it alone as the umpire calls it a no ball but for overstepping.
Wide outside off, Ramdin defends it.
Ramdin shoulders arms to let that one through.
DENESH RAMDIN is the new man in.

OUT! Another one bites the dust. Samuels is the man who trudges back to the hut. Full length delivery on middle and leg, Samuels looks to close the face of his bat and work it to the leg side. He is too early as the ball catches the leading edge and lobs in the air to the off side. Bailey at short cover takes the simplest of the catches to hand Marsh his second wicket. Not much to worry for WI but 204 runs is a long way to go. Okay, a little bit of pressure then!
Shortish around off, Charles punches it to covers off his back foot. A wild thow at the keeper is fumbled by Wade but no extra run is conceded.
Charles pushes it to covers for no runs.
Pitched up on off, driven straight down the ground. Zampa dives to his left and saves valuable runs.
Samuels defends the floated delivery to square leg.
Loopy delivery on off, Marlon bat-pads that one. A half-appeal for LBW is turned down.
FOUR! Precise! Short and around off, no spin on that one. Samuels builds his confidence as he slices it late through backward point for a boundary.
Good length around off, pushed to covers for a run to end the over. Just two off it but the all-important scalp of Bravo as well.
Wide outside off, run down to third man for a run.
Shortish outside off, Samuels downs his wrists and lets it through. Marsh fell on the pitch on his followthrough on that occasion.
Samuels shoulders arms to let that one through.
MARLON SAMUELS is in next.

OUT! Edged and Wade takes it easily! Back of a length outside off. The last match hero, Darren Bravo goes for a nothing shot, a loose poke to the off side but only garners a soft outside edge to it. Wade collects it and that's the end of the southpaw. Bravo walks back today without giving much trouble and Aussies are right on top now. A forlorn-faced DB walks back as Marsh celebrates his first wicket of the game. With that the players take a bit of rest with West Indies needing more 209 runs to win.
Full and on middle, Charles flicks it away to deep backward square leg for a single.
Shortish on middle, Charles camps back and punches it to long on for a single to end the over.
Loopy around off, Charles opens the face of his bat and guides it to point. Looks at his partner for a run but Bravo doesn't look interested.
On middle and leg, defended to short mid-wicket.
Leg spinner on off, Charles blocks it watchfully.
Shortish around off, punched to the off side for no run.
Yorker on off, Charles digs it out back to Zampa.
WIDE! Starts with a flighted and fuller delivery way down the leg side. Charles fails to flick and Wade collects it nicely to clip the bails off.
ADAM ZAMPA comes into the attack for the very first time.
Fuller length around off, Bravo mistimes it to mid off, yet again. Another tidy over!
Back of a length on off, nipping away. Bravo is amazed with the away swing as he lets it through.
On off, pushed straight to mid off. No run on offer there.
Good length on off, the ball goes off the inside half of his bat and rolls to square leg.
Wide outside off, driven through covers for a single.
Back of a length around off, pulled away to mid-wicket for a run.
A replica of the last delivery. Bravo hangs his bat and watches the ball travel to Wade.
Landed outside off, shaped in. Bravo lets it through again.
Good length delivery on off, Bravo closes the face of his bat and works it to the leg side. He sets off but gets back in as Marsh gets to the ball in a flash. Sensible!
Darren shoulders arms to let that one through. That should have been a wide.
Delicate glance by Charles through the fine leg region for a run.

Short ball on off, Charles goes for a pull. Unlike before he fails to connect this time and surrisingly Wade goes up in a caught behind appeal. Nothing from Marsh and it is called one bouncer for the over.
Short of a length around off, Bravo arches back and lets it through to Wade.
FOUR! Wow! Back of a length outside off, poor delivery from NCN. Bravo enjoys the line, length and the room provided as he flushes it with a pull through mid-wicket for his first boundary.
On middle and off, driven to long on for a single.
Shortish outside off, Charles waits for it to cut and does so easily. The only problem, ends up playing it straight to Maxwell at point.
On a length around off, JC blocks it nicely.
Charles shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
NATHAN COULTER-NILE comes back on.
A replica of the last delivery. A MAIDEN for Marsh to start with!
Fullish outside off, Bravo lifts his arms to it.
Full on off, pushed to mid on for a naught.
Full and wide outside off, Bravo shoulders his arms to it.
Bravo pushes the good length delivery to covers for no run.
Short and on off, Bravo dances down the track and half-pulls it to mid on for no run.
MITCHELL MARSH is into the attack now.
Serves it on the pads now, Bravo tucks it to mid-wicket to get off the mark with a single.
Landed on off, Bravo pushes it to the off side.
On a length around off, Bravo defends it.
DARREN BRAVO walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! That wasn't needed as Charles was going beserk at the other end! Fletcher's misery ends! A back of a length delivery outside off, Fletcher dances down the track but ends up slicing it. The ball catches the outside edge and travels straight to first slip. Smith hangs on to that with a reverse-cup catch and unknowingly throws the ball at the stumps looking at Fletcher outside the crease. The Aussie captain then realises it's a catch and celebrates with his teammates. First success for Australia and WI now need 222 runs for victory!
Wide outside off, in a swift wrist action Charles runs it down to third man for a single.
On a length around off, Charles takes it easy this time and blocks it watchfully.
POWERPLAY 2! Four fielders are allowed outside the circle now.

FOUR! Beauty! Full and wide outside off, Fletcher ends the Powerplay in style, leaning into the ball and driving it through the covers for a boundary! This has been an intelligent start from the home side.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, 137.1 kph, punched off the back foot.
Goes back and quietly tucks it through square leg for a single.

FOUR! He is growing in confidence now. A length ball around middle, 135 kph, Charles comes down the track and heaves it through mid-wicket. There is no one in the deep and that is a boundary. 228 more needed from 245 balls now.
Back of a length outside off, 132.1 kph, Fletcher comes forward, then goes back and punches it to point.
A length ball outside off, 136.7 kph, Johnson gets across and nudges it through square leg for a single.
Full and outside off, 137 kph, driven uppishly towards mid off.
Full and outside off, 135 kph, well defended.
This is outside off, angled in, 138.8 kph, left alone.
FOUR! Awesome! Full and outside off, Charles leans and drives it through covers for a boundary!

Full on middle 131.1 kph, Charles works it towards Mitchell Starc at mid on. They go for a quick single and the pacer has a shy at the bowler's end and hits them too. The ball deflects away to the bowler. Ahem... replays show that Charles did not ground his bat. Had the throw hit the stumps a second earlier, Charles would have been on his way back.
Outside off, 139.4 kph, pushed straight to Glenn Maxwell at point.
Another one at 137.7 kph, tapped to point for a quick single. The fielder comes running in, dives and has an underarm shy at the bowler's end but misses. Fletcher was in though.
A short ball outside off, 137.7 kph, angling in, Fletcher looks to pull but misses. The ball just goes past the inside edge over the stumps.
Full on middle and off, flicked straight to mid on.
On a good length around off, 136.3 kph, defended watchfully.

FOUR! Amazing! Short and outside off, 135.7 kph, Charles punches it into the ground between point and cover and gets a boundary! That breaks the shackles, 10 from it. 239 more needed from 258 balls now.
Similar ball, 135.4 kph, pushed to mid off again.
Full and outside off, pushed defensively to mid off.
Usman Khawaja now moves from deep backward square leg to deep mid-wicket.
SIX! First biggie of the chase! Slightly short in length outside off, 134.3 kph, Charles is ready for it and pulls it over mid-wicket for a biggie!
On a good length around off, angling in, 134.4 kph, Charles looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the hips.
Full and outside off, coming in, 132.8 kph, pushed towards mid on.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD has a change of ends.
Landed outside off, 135.7 kph, steered to third man for a run. 249 more needed from 264 balls now.
Outside off, 138.7 kph, pushed back to the bowler.
Length ball outside off, 132.4 kph, pulled through square leg for a couple.
A length ball outside off, Fletcher whips it through square leg where Adam Zampa dives and parries it away. A single taken. Three saved.
Another short ball, this is pull-worked to deep square leg for a single.
A short ball outside off, Charles looks to pull but the ball goes off his thighs to second slip.
NATHAN COULTER-NILE to bowl now.
Full and outside off, 147.4 kph, Charles steers it slightly off the outside edge to third man for a run.
Excellent inswinger, nearly gets it through, 145.5 kph, Fletcher pushes it to covers for a single.
Full and outside off, 141.7 kph, Andre looks to drive but misses. Starc has some words to say to Fletcher who doesn't respond. Perhaps he was asking about the dessert after lunch.

HUGE LBW APPEAL, TURNED DOWN! Starc wants a review but Smith shakes his head. Good call. Will tell you why. Full and outside off, swings back in, 146.2 kph, Fletcher misses his swing and is hit on the pads. That looks a dead duck but the umpire shakes his head. Starc pleads for the wicket but it is not heeded. The Australian captain indicates that there was an inside edge. Replays indicate the same. Top class decision.
On a good length around middle and off, angling away, 144.6 kph, pushed defensively to point.
WIDE. That is the third one from Starc already and he is really struggling with the away angle to the right-hander. Bowls it wide outside off, fuller in length, 143.1 kph, Fletcher lets it through.
Full and outside off, 144.3 kph, watchfully defended towards point.
Landed outside off, angling in, 131.1 kph, JC looks to pull-flick but misses and the ball goes off his thighs, on the bounce to the keeper. A MAIDEN from Hazlewood.
Outside off, punched straight to point.
Full and outside off, 135.5 kph, watchfully defended.

Similar to the first ball. Bowled on a good length, outside off, 132.2 kph, nipping back in, Johnson misses his tuck again and is hit on the pads. Hazlewood has a look at the pitch, then at the batsman and then wipes his lips with his hand. Looks like he is trying to identify a spot there.
Outside off, on a good length, 130.8 kph, punched back to the bowler.
Good length ball on middle, 143.2 kph, Charles misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Ooohhh... a teaser outside off, 143.2 kph, fuller in length, Andre looks to drive but is beaten.
Full and outside off, 144.6 kph, Fletcher takes his bat out of the way.

DROPPED! But a tough chance. Full and outside off, Charles looks to drive without moving his feet and gets a thick outside edge behind. Steven Smith is airborne, flings himself to his right from second slip but is unable to hold on with his right hand. Parries it to third man and the batsmen take a single.
Full and wide outside off, driven straight to cover who dives to his left and parries it to point.
WIDE. Full and wide outside off, 140.8 kph, comfortable leave.

Full on middle, 141.2 kph, swinging in, Charles whips it across the line through square leg but Adam Zampa over there dives to his right and half-stops the ball. Two runs taken. 259 more needed from 287 balls now.
Down the leg side, 129.3 kph, worked to fine leg for a single to keep the strike.
Full and outside off, 130.1 kph, left alone.

Overcompensates by bowling too straight, 134.3 kph, Johnson tucks it through fine leg. The ball races away to the fence but Usman Khawaja gets across to his right and dives to pull the ball back in. Two runs taken.
FOUR! That was really well played. Short and outside off, 132.3 kph, Charles slaps it behind point and beats third man comfortably.
Full on middle, 130.3 kph, flicked straight to square leg.
On a good length outside off, 138 kph, tapped to Glenn Maxwell at point.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD to bowl with the second new ball.
Landed outside off, left alone again to end the over.
WIDE. Full and outside off, 143.4 kph, angling away, left alone.
Full and swinging in, 143.9 kph, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, 142.5 kph, Andre comes forward and blocks it to point.

Swings back in a long way from outside off, fuller in length, Fletcher flicks it through mid-wicket. Fletcher thinks it will go all the way but the man at square leg dives to his left and gets some hand to it. That slows down the ball and Josh Hazlewood gets to the ball from deep backward square leg. Just 2 runs taken. Should have been 3. 268 more needed from 297 balls.
Full and outside off, 143.8 kph, left alone.
Oohhh... what a start. Full and outside off, 142.9 kph, Fletcher does not want to waste any time, swings wildly but the ball swings back in and beats the inside edge.

Welcome back for the run chase. 271 needed for West Indies to win their first ever final in ODIs since the 2004 Champions Trophy against full member nations. Can they end their title drought tonight? The players are back out in the middle. Johnson Charles and Andre Fletcher are the openers for the home side. Mitchell Starc to start off proceedings against Fletcher. Here we go...
